original_question: (W. Willems). Conjecture: The sum of squares of the degrees of the irreducible p-Brauer characters of a finite group G is at least the p′-part of |G|. This is known to be true for p = 2(G. Malle, Adv. Math., 380(2021), Paper no. 107609, 15 pp.).
target_in_paper: Open Problem 21.91 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)".
correct_elements: Your draft already reproduces the paper's official formulation almost verbatim: it identifies Willems's conjecture, states the inequality for the sum of squares of the degrees of irreducible p-Brauer characters of a finite group G, and includes the paper's note that the case p = 2 is known by a result of G. Malle.
missing_details: The quantifiers should be made explicit: the question is intended for every prime p and every finite group G.
The sum should be written explicitly as running over all irreducible p-Brauer characters, for example over φ in IBr_p(G).
The term "degree" should be identified as the value φ(1).
The notation "the p′-part of |G|" should be defined as the largest divisor of |G| that is coprime to p, usually written |G|_{p′}.

If one wants the question to be fully stand-alone, one should specify that p-Brauer characters are understood in the standard modular representation-theoretic sense, e.g. over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p; the paper leaves this background implicit.
It is worth stating explicitly that the paper imposes no further hypotheses on G beyond finiteness.
refined_question: For every prime p and every finite group G, let IBr_p(G) denote the set of irreducible p-Brauer characters of G (in the usual modular representation-theoretic sense over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p), and let |G|_{p′} denote the largest divisor of |G| that is coprime to p. Must one always have sum_{φ in IBr_p(G)} φ(1)^2 >= |G|_{p′}? The paper notes that this is known when p = 2.
justification: The arXiv source here is the Kourovka Notebook, so the nearest official formulation is not a theorem or section-1 conjecture but the open problem numbered 21.91. Your draft matches that problem essentially word for word. Nearby context adds only the note that the conjecture is known for p = 2, and the paper does not provide a separate equivalent reformulation or extra hypotheses at this location. The necessary refinement is therefore just to make the standard notation and quantifiers fully explicit while staying faithful to Problem 21.91.
